name: Applied Philosophy of Quantum Theory
description: Quantum computers are expected to progress from today’s noisy intermediate-scale quantum devices (NISQ) to fault-tolerant architectures. Alongside this hardware development, advances in quantum algorithms exploit superposition, interference, and entanglement to speed up certain computational tasks. This course introduces the foundations of quantum information and computation and develops core quantum algorithmic ideas in several contexts – from search and amplitude amplification to techniques used in quantum learning. We will explore how these algorithms operate, what resources they require, and when they can offer practical or theoretical advantages over classical approaches.
prerequisites: Basic knowledge of Python and linear algebra.
